reason: `context.clearCookies({ name: /coo.*1/ })` removes the cookies whose name matches a regular expression. Strider's `cookies.remove` takes an exact name, so the pattern has no form and the test can't be ported

`context.clearCookies({ domain })` removes every cookie for a domain, whatever its name. Strider's `cookies.remove` requires a name, so a domain alone has no form, and porting it would clear by name instead

`context.clearCookies({ path })` removes every cookie for a path, whatever its name. Strider's `cookies.remove` requires a name, so a path alone has no form, and porting it would clear by name instead
Upstream skips this test on every browser but Chromium: partitioned cookies (CHIPS) are Chromium-specific

The test's context accepts the fixture's self-signed certificate (`ignoreHTTPSErrors`), which Chromium refuses per context with `acceptInsecureCerts`, as browsercontext-add-cookies' CO-041 is. Its removal by name also has no partition key in Strider's `Match`
